name: Tagsmith
description: Derives searchable, machine-readable tags (origin=, lang=, year= ...) from metadata Jellyfin already holds, and keeps them in sync as the library changes.
overview: Automatic namespaced metadata tags for Jellyfin.

versions.changelog:
## Tagsmith v0.0.4

### Breaking

- **Country tags in the  namespace will be rewritten on the first run after upgrading.** The new country canonicalisation is on by default. Every spelling of a country now resolves to one canonical English slug: , , , and  all become ;  becomes ;  becomes . If you had  or any other non-canonical form, it will be replaced. Turn off *Canonicalise country names* in the settings page to tag the raw metadata value instead and preserve the old behaviour.

- **Pruning now covers every prefix Tagsmith has ever written, not just currently active ones.** The plugin records all managed prefixes in a new  configuration list. Tags under a prefix that is no longer active — because you renamed a namespace or turned one off — are cleaned up on the next run rather than left behind. The list is visible and editable on the settings page: delete a line to make Tagsmith stop managing tags with that prefix permanently.

### Added

- **Collections projection: tag namespaces can now be browsed as a library of collections.** Enabling *Project origins*, *Project languages*, or *Project years* creates a Jellyfin library (named Origins, Languages, or Decades by default) whose collections are built from the tags. Every client can browse the collections without knowing tags exist. Tags remain the source of truth and collections are rebuilt from them on each run. Off by default.

- **Year tags project by decade rather than by individual year.**  stays precise as a tag, but the year projection groups items into , , and so on — ten tiles rather than a hundred.

- **Hand-set collection posters are adopted and preserved.** Set a poster on a collection in the Jellyfin UI and Tagsmith copies it into  as the stored artwork for that value, so it survives the collection being rebuilt. The folder also works in the other direction: drop a file there and it is applied to the matching collection. A hash guards both directions so a run with nothing changed writes nothing.

- **If a projection library is deleted in Jellyfin's own settings, Tagsmith treats that as intent and does not recreate it.** The corresponding projection is switched off in config automatically.

- **User alias rules.** A new *Aliases* field on the settings page accepts free-form rewrite rules applied after canonicalisation:  rewrites within one namespace,  applies everywhere, and an empty replacement drops the tag. Lines starting with  are comments. A malformed line is skipped rather than breaking a scan.

- **A starter set of collection artwork is published in  in the repository.** Flag posters for 7 origin countries, native-script language cards for 31 languages (English, French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, and all 22 languages of the Indian constitution's Eighth Schedule), and decade cards from the 1920s to the 2020s. Not bundled in the plugin; copy what you want into the thumbnails directory.

- **Historical states — Soviet Union, Yugoslavia, West Germany, Czechoslovakia — are deliberately not mapped by country canonicalisation.** They pass through as  and so on rather than being folded into successor states. Add an alias rule if you want different behaviour.

### Fixed

- **Renaming a namespace or changing the separator no longer leaves orphaned tags.** Previously, changing  to  would stop managing the old  tags; they would remain on every item indefinitely. The  mechanism ensures the old prefix is still pruned on subsequent runs.

### Internal

- Sub-task progress reporting now reserves the last 10% for the collection projection phase, rather than reaching 100% before projection starts.
- Elapsed time is logged separately for the tagging pass and the projection pass so performance can be measured.
- , , , and  are new;  registers  as a singleton.
- Claude agent definitions added for the commit-message, release-notes, test, and validate workflow steps.

**Compatibility:** Jellyfin 10.11.11 (). Unchanged since v0.0.2.
